resources.string: Instagram, the way it used to be.
Only the people you follow and care about.
Set it up now, or any time later in Settings.
15, 30 or 45 minutes a day. Messages stay open when it\'s up, and calls never count.
A few seconds with a question or a quote each time you open it. On from the start; you can switch it off.
Time spent, what\'s left today, and what was removed for you.
A calmer way into Instagram, not a new account.
No account, no tracking, no analytics. Nothing leaves your phone except Instagram\'s own traffic.
You log in on Instagram\'s own page. Throwback never sees your password.
The code is public on GitHub.
There\'s no extra button on your feed.
Press and hold the Home tab at the bottom for a moment, and Throwback\'s settings open: your daily limit, the pause, Your day and the Instagram app connection.
The tab bar at the bottom of Instagram, with the Home tab held down.
Free. Not affiliated with Instagram or Meta.
Log in with your Instagram account
You still have the Instagram app
It\'s the quickest way back to Reels. What do you want to do with it?
For calls, message alerts and posting. Throwback keeps you out of everything else.
Opens the app\'s page in Android Settings. Tap Uninstall there.
You can change this anytime in Settings → Connect → Instagram.
Your feed and stories, from the people you follow. These are always on. That\'s the point.
Lock Throwback after a set time each day
A short pause before Instagram opens
Your own name and icon on the home screen
Instagram only sends notifications to its own app. So the real app stays on your phone, and Throwback keeps you out of it. Log in to the Instagram app with the same account you use in Throwback.
Calls ring and you answer normally
Post and add stories with Instagram\'s own editor
Open the Instagram app outside a call and Throwback brings you back
Install the Instagram app from the Play Store
The Instagram app is on this phone, so opening it would skip your daily limit. Connect Instagram to Throwback, and Throwback covers it.
Step 2 asks for three Android permissions, each explained there. Throwback needs them to pass on Instagram\'s notifications and keep you out of its app.
Step 2 asks for four Android permissions, each explained there. Throwback needs them to pass on Instagram\'s notifications and keep you out of its app.
Only the Instagram app in your main profile is covered. A second copy (in a work profile, a phone\'s dual apps or Private Space) isn\'t.
Throwback reads them to pass on messages, ring your calls and see when a story is posted. In Instagram\'s notification settings, keep both groups on. Throwback hides the ones you don\'t need.
Working: Throwback has seen them this week.
None from the \'Instagram\' group in 7 days. Check that it\'s on.
Posting a story, likes, follows and more
To show you Instagram\'s messages as Throwback\'s own
Each opens an Android screen. Turn Throwback on there, then come back.
To pass on messages and calls, and drop the rest
To notice when the Instagram app opens
To cover the Instagram app and bring you back
Throwback only looks at the Instagram app. Nothing leaves your phone; only daily counts are kept on it.

Android guards this for apps installed from a downloaded file instead of an app store. Open App info, tap ⋮ at the top right, then \"Allow restricted settings\", and turn on Notification access again.
Throwback can\'t show notifications, so Instagram\'s own message notifications stay as they are. You can allow it later in Android\'s settings.
Messages come from Throwback. The Instagram app opens for calls and posting; anything else brings you back
Install it for calls, message alerts and posting
Posting: “+” and “Your story” open Instagram\'s editor
Off: likes, comments, followers and more
Everything you leave off is removed before you see it.
It happens 24 hours from now, tomorrow at %1$s. Until then the Instagram app stays covered, as it is now. You can cancel any time before.
Couldn\'t open that picture. Try another one.
Support Throwback once, any amount, and Make It Yours unlocks for good. Try it out below.
Call it whatever you like and use any picture. Throwback doesn\'t use Instagram\'s name or logo, but your shortcut is yours. Most phones add a small Throwback badge to shortcuts.
Sent to your home screen. Your phone may ask you to confirm.
Your home screen app can\'t add shortcuts. Try long-pressing Throwback in your app list instead.

string-array.name: ui_pause_quotes
string-array.item: What is this life if, full of care, / We have no time to stand and stare.|W. H. Davies, “Leisure” (1911)
Why should we live with such hurry and waste of life?|Henry David Thoreau, Walden (1854)
As if you could kill time without injuring eternity.|Henry David Thoreau, Walden (1854)
The question is not what you look at, but what you see.|Henry David Thoreau, Journal (1851)
Try to be one of the people on whom nothing is lost!|Henry James, “The Art of Fiction” (1884)
Why should not we also enjoy an original relation to the universe?|Ralph Waldo Emerson, Nature (1836)
Write it on your heart that every day is the best day in the year.|Ralph Waldo Emerson, “Works and Days” (1870)
Leave this military hurry and adopt the pace of Nature.|Ralph Waldo Emerson, “Education” (1883)
You need a change of soul rather than a change of climate.|Seneca, Letters to Lucilius, tr. Richard M. Gummere (1917)
Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years.|Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, tr. George Long (1862)
First, say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.|Epictetus, Discourses, tr. Thomas W. Higginson (1890)
If not now when?|Hillel, Pirkei Avot, tr. Charles Taylor (1897)
Seize the present; trust to-morrow e’en as little as you may.|Horace, Odes, tr. John Conington (1863)
Remember then: there is only one time that is important—Now!|Leo Tolstoy, “Three Questions”, tr. Louise and Aylmer Maude (1906)
Go into yourself.|Rainer Maria Rilke, Letters to a Young Poet, tr. M. D. Herter Norton (1934)
Live the questions now.|Rainer Maria Rilke, Letters to a Young Poet, tr. M. D. Herter Norton (1934)
All we have to decide is what to do with the time that is given us.|J. R. R. Tolkien, The Fellowship of the Ring (1954)
Tell me, what is it you plan to do with your one wild and precious life?|Mary Oliver, “The Summer Day” (1990)
Instructions for living a life: Pay attention. Be astonished. Tell about it.|Mary Oliver, “Sometimes” (2008)
Be joyful though you have considered all the facts.|Wendell Berry, “Manifesto: The Mad Farmer Liberation Front” (1973)
Practice resurrection.|Wendell Berry, “Manifesto: The Mad Farmer Liberation Front” (1973)
Ask the questions that have no answers.|Wendell Berry, “Manifesto: The Mad Farmer Liberation Front” (1973)
So, friends, every day do something that won’t compute.|Wendell Berry, “Manifesto: The Mad Farmer Liberation Front” (1973)
If something is boring after two minutes, try it for four.|John Cage, Silence (1961)
Get busy living or get busy dying.|Stephen King, “Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption” (1982)
If you don’t stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.|Ferris Bueller’s Day Off (1986)
Carpe diem. Seize the day, boys. Make your lives extraordinary.|Dead Poets Society (1989)
Look for the helpers. You will always find people who are helping.|Fred Rogers, on his mother’s advice
Be Here Now|Ram Dass, book title (1971)
Don’t Just Do Something, Sit There|Sylvia Boorstein, book title (1996)
What Would You Do If You Weren’t Afraid?|Spencer Johnson, Who Moved My Cheese? (1998)
If you’re not saying “HELL YEAH!” about something, say no.|Derek Sivers, sive.rs (2009)
Be a mystery, not a demographic.|Matt Haig, Notes on a Nervous Planet (2018)
What would this look like if it were easy?|Tim Ferriss, The Tim Ferriss Show (2016)

string-array.item: Long-press Home to open Throwback\'s settings.

string-array.name: ui_pause_lines
string-array.item: Take a breath. The people you follow will still be here in a moment.
You opened this on purpose. What did you come to see?
Catch up with your people, then get back to your day.
Could this be a short visit today?
Look up for a moment. Then decide.
Check in on your friends, not on the feed.
Say hello, see what\'s new, and leave while it still feels good.
Drink some water first. Seriously.
Who do you actually want to see today?
Who\'s in charge today: you, or your thumb?
Would five good minutes be enough today?
Is there someone you could just text instead?
Sit up, roll your shoulders back. Okay, go.
What were you doing before you picked up your phone?
Notice one thing around you that isn\'t a screen.
Come for your friends. Leave before it gets boring.
What\'s been the best part of your day so far?
One look, then back to life.
Remember when this was just photos of friends? It still is.
Breathe in for four. Out for four. There.
Close it whenever you like. That\'s the whole trick.
Is someone nearby who\'d like a chat more than a like?
Pick one thing to check, then put it down.
When you reach the end of the feed, let that be the end.
Go easy on yourself today.
Window open? Sky still there? Good.
Like, comment, leave. The classic.
Bored? Stay with it for a minute. What idea turns up?
Your morning, your evening: what are your rules?
See your people. Skip the noise.
